chain.label: King Air crew did not monitor or transmit on CTAF
chain.trigger: the failure of the pilots in the King Air A90 to effectively monitor the common traffic advisory frequency

chain.label: King Air crew failed to scan for and see the landing Beech 1900C
chain.trigger: or to properly scan for traffic

chain.label: Cherokee pilot's unnecessary interrupted transmission answered flight 5925's query to the King Air, uncorrected
chain.trigger: the Cherokee pilot's transmission in response to flight 5925's request was unnecessary and inappropriate and, combined with the lack of any correction to the flight crew's misunderstanding, misled the flight crew

chain.label: 1900C crew mistakenly believed the King Air would hold on the runway
chain.trigger: they mistook the Cherokee pilot's transmission (that he was holding for departure on runway 4) as a response from the King Air ... and therefore mistakenly believed that the King Air was not planning to take off until after flight 5925 had cleared the runway

caused_by.evidence: the Cherokee pilot's interrupted radio transmission, which led to the Beech 1900C pilot's misunderstanding of the transmission as an indication from the King Air that it would not take off

chain.label: King Air began takeoff roll on runway 4 while the 1900C was landing on intersecting runway 13
chain.trigger: resulting in their commencing a takeoff roll when the Beech 1900C (United Express flight 5925) was landing on an intersecting runway

caused_by.evidence: the King Air A90 flight crew failed to announce its takeoff intentions on the common traffic advisory frequency, which was required by the AIM
the King Air A90 pilots' failure to announce the airplane's takeoff over the common traffic advisory frequency and yield to the landing airplane (which had the right of way) led to the accident

chain.label: No staffed on-airport aircraft rescue and firefighting service at Quincy
chain.trigger: Although Quincy Municipal Airport had an ARFF truck, it was not staffed at the time of the accident because no air carrier aircraft with more than 30 passenger seats were taking off or landing

chain.label: Beech 1900C and King Air A90 collided at the runway intersection
chain.trigger: United Express flight 5925, a Beechcraft 1900C, N87GL, and a Beechcraft King Air A90, N1127D, collided at Quincy Municipal Airport ... The collision occurred at the intersection of the two runways

caused_by.evidence: commencing a takeoff roll when the Beech 1900C ... was landing on an intersecting runway
the 1900C pilots may have been less concerned about continuing to watch the King Air A90 during their landing

chain.label: Intense fuel-fed post-impact pool fire enveloped both airplanes
chain.trigger: The speed with which the fire enveloped the King Air and the intensity of the fire precluded survivability for the occupants of the King Air

caused_by.evidence: the occupants' fatal injuries were associated with the pool fire which ultimately ignited the interior

chain.label: 1900C air stair door not opened, from inside or by two rescuers; overwing exit also unopened
chain.trigger: the air stair door and the left overwing exit hatch were not opened for undetermined reasons ... neither was able to open the door

chain.label: All 14 occupants of both airplanes died of smoke inhalation and thermal injuries despite survivable impact
chain.trigger: The 2 flight crewmembers and all 10 passengers aboard the 1900C were killed, and the 2 occupants aboard the King Air A90 were killed

caused_by.evidence: the cause of death for the occupants of both airplanes was either 'carbon monoxide intoxication from inhalation of smoke and soot' from the postimpact fire or 'inhalation of products of combustion'
the 1900C occupants succumbed to inhalation and thermal injuries because they did not escape from the airplane using the two available exits—one of which was the air stair door
ARFF personnel might have been able to extinguish or control the fire, thereby extending the survival time for at least some of the 1900C occupants
